newsitem.title: UK: Racal considers data products float.
newsitem.headline: Racal considers data products float.

text.p: Racal Electronics Plc said on Thursday it was considering a partial flotation of its U.S. data products business on either Nasdaq or the New York Stock Exchange.

David Elsbury, group chief executive, said in an interview that a decision would be made on whether to float the division by March 1998 at the latest. Separately, Elsbury said the group was also in talks with a number of potential partners for its telecommunications division.

The two initiatives form part of efforts by the defence electronic group to restore shareholder value after reporting two profit warnings since December and a slump in its share price over the last year.
On June 3 the company announced a strategic review to refocus on its three main businesses -- telecoms, data products and defence electronics.
Elsbury said the company has appointed Goldman Sachs "to see whether flotation is the right way forward".

"We can't float less than 20 percent (under U.S. regulations). We have four options in all, keep it, close it as we will never be able to get it right, partially float it or form a joint venture with another company."
On the telecoms side he said the company was in talks with a number of parties about establishing a partnership. These partners fell into four categories, said Elsbury.

Global partners looking to enter the UK market where Racal Telecoms is second to British Telecommunications Plc. "Country bound" telecom players seeking to expand abroad, as well as UK start up telecom companies and information providers.
Asked whether AT&T Corp was one of the parties he said "they are all talking to us."
Elsbury said the key feature was that the telecoms partner should be able to deliver an overseas network.
